# Introduction

This file is used to conduct basic correlation analysis on recreational fishers in the 2025 SELTMP data. Pearson's and Spearman's Analysis are conducted between

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# R Setup & housekeeping
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
	echo = TRUE,
	include = TRUE,
	message = FALSE,
	warning = FALSE)

rm(list=ls())
objects()
```

```{r}
# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(datarium) #Pearson's correlation matrices
```

# 1. Prepare data

```{r}
# Import Raw Data sheet
raw_data <- read_excel(here::here("Data/SELTMP-2025-GBR-surveydataset_v1-0_RecFishingCLUSTERS_RyanW-Oct-22-2026.xlsx"), sheet = "Raw_Data")

#glimpse(raw_data)
```

```{r}
# Filter Data for only Rec Fishers
fisher_data <- raw_data |> filter(Are_you_a_Rec_Fisher == 1)
nrow(fisher_data)
```

# Select variables and set all as numeric

```{r}
# Switch variables to numeric for test
fisher_data$inter_zoning <- as.numeric(as.character(fisher_data$inter_zoning))
fisher_data$educ         <- as.numeric(as.character(fisher_data$educ))
```

### Pearson's Test

Note: r = 0 to 0.30; negligible correlation r = 0.30 to 0.50; moderate correlation r = 0.50 to 1 highly correlated

```{r}
cor.test(fisher_data$inter_zoning, fisher_data$educ)
```

### Alternative: Spearman's Test (rank based)

```{r}
cor.test(fisher_data$inter_zoning, fisher_data$educ, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```
